title: How to choose the right bandana for your pet
excerpt: Neck measurement, shape, fastening, fabric and colour — the seven decisions that make a bandana sit like it belongs there.
seo_description: A practical guide to choosing a pet bandana: how to measure the neck, which shape suits which breed, tie-on vs slip-on, the right fabric, and how to pick a colour that flatters your pet's coat.

title: Where to actually put a sticker (and where not to)
excerpt: Vinyl sticks to things that are smooth, hard, clean and dry. Everything else is a negotiation.
seo_description: A practical guide to applying vinyl stickers: which surfaces work, which never will, how to prep in ten seconds, how to apply without bubbles, and how to remove one cleanly.

title: Getting the size right, first time
excerpt: A tape measure, five centimetres and thirty seconds. Plus the three sizing mistakes almost everyone makes.
seo_description: How to measure your pet for a bandana: the exact method, a breed-by-breed size guide from XS to XL, the three most common sizing mistakes, and how it should look once it's on.

title: How to wash a bandana without wrecking the print
excerpt: Cold water, inside out, and never the tumble dryer. Everything that keeps printed colour bright for years.
seo_description: How to wash a printed pet bandana so the colours last: the right temperature, why fabric softener and tumble drying ruin prints, and how to handle mud, grass and drool stains.

title: How a drawing becomes a sticker, a print and a keyring
excerpt: The drawing takes twenty minutes. Everything after the drawing takes a fortnight. Here is the whole route.
seo_description: Behind the scenes of a small illustration shop: how a doodle is redrawn, adapted for stickers, prints, pins and fabric, proofed, cut, checked and packed.

title: Ten categories, and how each one started
excerpt: None of it was a plan. Every category began as one drawing that got out of hand.
seo_description: The story behind the ten Julia Mind categories — ducks, mushrooms, frogs, snails, bees, cats, bears, strawberries, moons and tiny snacks — and how each one started.
